The T=0.7 Dawid-Skene fit did NOT consume the 4,745 layer: it consumed the fixed 4,770 base. The sentence bundles three commits (366f9c66f D-S re-aggregate, e07dae373 cross-tab, f533fda5f re-evaluate) and the '4,745' is true of f533fda5f (the evaluation) but false of 366f9c66f (the D-S re-aggregation), so the compression misattributes the reference.

evidence: scripts/analyse_dawid_skene.py:57 — _STUDENT_GT_PATH defaults to inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps.geojson, the fixed 4,770 base (ruling 19 layer 1).
Count test: item-posteriors.csv student_label==1 rows give 4,770 for T=0.7, T=0.3 and text-MIN, and 4,745 for image — exactly the base and the reviewed layer's size between baf1497a7 and 2e075eb99.

In T=0.7 the same coordinate carries student_label=0 (category vlm_only), i.e. the curator addition was absent from the T=0.7 reference set.

Commit 366f9c66f's own message asserts the D-S re-run used 'the canonical student GT (now including the +1 curator-added mound at K-35-064-3, baf1497a7)'. The artefact contradicts the commit message; the document inherited the commit message's error.
confirmed_defects_unrepaired.the_documents_own_contradiction: Lines 189-194 of the same document already state the correct fact — 'the corrected-f1 pipeline using the *reviewed* student GT at multi-buffer rings while D-S uses the legacy student GT at 50 m'. The front matter contradicts § 3 of its own body. What neither passage records is that IMAGE is the exception to its own rule.
confirmed_defects_unrepaired.interpretive_consequence: UNADJUDICATED — flagged, not decided. The image run's D-S reference is 25 student points smaller than its three siblings', so every cross-run D-S comparison in this document (§ 2.1 item counts, § 2.2 worker accuracy and prevalence, § 4.1 F1 ranking, § 4.2 calibration ranking) compares image against the other three on a different reference. § 4.1's D-S F1 gap between image (0.7990) and T=0.3 (0.7988) is 0.0002 — far smaller than the plausible effect of removing 25 student double-marks, which mechanically reduces student_only (false negatives) and so raises recall. The document already calls that ordering noise-level ('preserved at 4 d.p. only as 0.7745 ≈ 0.7743 within rounding'); this finding adds that the two runs are not on a common reference at all, so the image-vs-T=0.3 rank order is not established by these artefacts.
confirmed_defects_unrepaired.relationship_to_W7_D8: The MIRROR IMAGE of W7-D8 and easy to conflate. W7-D8 is about the EVALUATION layer, where t0.3 is the odd one out (unreviewed 4,770, siblings reviewed). W7-D9 is about the DAWID-SKENE layer, where IMAGE is the odd one out (reviewed 4,745, siblings the fixed 4,770 base). Different objects, different runs, opposite direction. W7-R1's history shows this pair has already caused one withdrawn claim.

(1) The t0.3 evaluation-layer difference is a NEW finding in its own right: any claim anchored to outputs/55maps-text-high-t0.3-generalisation/evaluation/ is on a different reference from its siblings, and t0.3 is the F1 leader in several places. resolution_of_open_question_2.question: Whether the four Dawid-Skene fits themselves share a ground-truth reference — a different object from the evaluation metadata the census read.
resolution_of_open_question_2.answer: They do NOT. Image alone consumed the reviewed curator layer (4,745 as it stood between baf1497a7 and 2e075eb99); T=0.7, T=0.3 and text-MIN all consumed the FIXED 4,770 base (ruling 19 layer 1), which is the script default.
resolution_of_open_question_2.the_blind_pass_was_right_about_the_split: Blind pass P4 put image at 4,745 and the other three at 4,770 — which is EXACTLY what the D-S fits show. The census then found the opposite locus (t0.3 odd-one-out at 4,770) and was read as inverting the blind pass. It did not: the census was reading EVALUATION metadata and the blind pass was reading D-S fits. Both were correct about their own object. Two different asymmetries exist, in different layers, singling out different runs.
evidence: scripts/analyse_dawid_skene.py:57 — the --ground-truth default is the fixed 4,770 base, so a run inherits 4,770 unless the operator overrode it.
item-posteriors.csv student_label==1 counts: 4,770 / 4,770 / 4,770 for T=0.7, T=0.3, text-MIN; 4,745 for image.

Decisive point test not relying on counts: baf1497a7's single added feature at (396492.2142937911, 4662802.316746469), K-35-064-3_Dimitrovgrad_4326, is a student point ONLY in the image item set; in T=0.7 that coordinate carries student_label=0.
resolution_of_open_question_2.consequence: Registered as document defect W7-D9, whose interpretive half (does § 4.1's image-vs-T=0.3 D-S F1 ordering survive?) is a PI call, not a bookkeeping repair.

open_research_findings.method_note: Worth keeping: the blind pass corrected the repair, the census corrected the blind pass, and Session 128 found the census and the blind pass were answering DIFFERENT questions and were each right. The lesson is not that one layer beat another but that 'which ground truth did this run use?' has to name the object — evaluation, D-S fit, or MCC — before it has an answer. Note also which evidence settled it: reading cli_args.ground_truth (census) and testing for one known-added POINT (Session 128) both beat inferring a reference from implied counts, which is what left the question open for a day.

instrument_gaps.severity: MEDIUM — recurs on every future repair
instrument_gaps.gap: `git_blob` pins a whole DOCUMENT while batches cover RANGES. Any edit anywhere in a document invalidates the recorded blob for EVERY batch covering it, including batches whose own lines never moved.
instrument_gaps.evidence: After the 2026-08-04 withdrawal at ~line 577 (inside b074's range), b073 failed validation on blob mismatch despite all 86 of its spans re-verifying verbatim, with its highest referenced line at 323.
instrument_gaps.why_it_now_matters: Charter rule 14 (ruling 18) makes document repair routine, so this will fire constantly.
instrument_gaps.cheap_answer_used_once: Repoint the blob after a verbatim re-check of every span (bc21ff3be). Re-extracting untouched ranges would be waste.
proper_fix_options: Record a per-batch range hash alongside the document blob, so an untouched range validates independently.
Have the validator treat a blob mismatch as satisfied when every span in the file re-verifies against the current body.
Formalise repointing as a supported operation with a recorded reason, rather than a hand edit.

instrument_gaps.gap: Sidecar metadata disagrees with its artefact. `results/gold-standard-extended-buffer-sweep/evaluation.json` records 10000 iterations / BCa while its co-located `evaluation.metadata.json` still records 1000 / percentile — and results/ci-metadata-registry.md designates the SIDECAR as its authority.

As it stands, a paper citing it would state the wrong bootstrap method (percentile rather than BCa) and the wrong iteration count (1000 rather than 10000) for these runs, and would point readers at several artefacts that are no longer where it says they are. instrument_gaps.next_step: Refresh the registry rows to the artefacts, repoint the archived paths, and either regenerate the surviving sidecars or retire them — a sidecar that no migration updates is a trap, not a record. Decide whether sidecars remain the registry's nominated authority at all.

measurement.registry_rows_bootstrap: All 4 registry rows naming a readable artefact disagree with it on bootstrap method — the registry says 'bootstrap percentile', the artefacts say BCa; where N is legible the registry says 1000 against 10000.

phantom_duplication_audit.method: Same-map nearest-neighbour from each of the 773 reviewer-promoted mounds (canonical-review.csv, EPSG:32635) to the corrected student GT (4,746, reprojected 4326->32635). Cross-map proximity excluded because the de-dup is same-map constrained.

promoted_vs_promoted.verdict: Internally unique. The 25 m and 50 m pairs are cross-map-unconstrained and consistent with genuinely adjacent mounds.

phantom_duplication_audit.verdict: Corroborates W6-E9 independently: exactly ONE true twin at 0.98 m, caught by the 5 m de-dup tolerance, consistent with the documented 1/2/2/0 per-pipeline drop counts. The promoted set is overwhelmingly well separated from the student layer — median nearest neighbour 115.7 m.
phantom_duplication_audit.residual_grey_zone: 4-6 cases sit between 7.3 m and 15 m — closer than the pipeline's own 'genuinely distinct mounds sit >=15-20 m apart' floor, further than the 5 m de-dup catches. Not resolvable from coordinates; they need visual adjudication on a map. FOLDED INTO the committed point-marking re-review (ruling 20c).
phantom_duplication_audit.open_question: canonical-review.csv holds 415 rows at buffer_metres=50 while the image run's summary records 474 promoted at R=50. Likely per-run phantom sets differing from the canonical adjudicated set, but UNVERIFIED.

metric_reference_asymmetry.finding: Corrected-F1 scores against the EXTENDED reference (4,746 student + per-buffer promoted phantoms: 5,220 at R=50 m, 5,418 at 150 m). Tile-level MCC scores against the student layer ALONE (4,746, 'no phantoms'), per the matrix-sweep convention documented in 55maps-mcc-v2-summary § 1.
metric_reference_asymmetry.why_it_matters: The F1-versus-MCC rank-divergence finding (Obs 280: text wins F1, image wins MCC) is measured across metrics that do not share a ground truth. An unknown share of that divergence could be reference effect rather than metric behaviour.
metric_reference_asymmetry.pi_ruling: Cannot go forward (ruling 20a). Both metrics must use the same reference.
metric_reference_asymmetry.sequencing: Do NOT recompute yet (ruling 20b) — the reference moves again at the phantom re-review, and recomputing twice is waste. Unification is gated on the point-marking work.
metric_reference_asymmetry.status: OPEN — gated, not deferred indefinitely. Blocks publication of the F1-vs-MCC divergence as a metric-behaviour claim.
metric_reference_asymmetry.nested_finding_2026_08_04: Found by the obs-writer while landing Obs 388, and NOT in the original analysis: the MCC side is not on 4,746 either. results/55maps-mcc-v2-summary § 1 records the GT file as 4,746 as at 2026-08-04, but § 2 states the MCC rows were computed against the canonical 4,745-mound curator GT (the 2026-05-03 evaluations). Under the era-disposition rule that § 2 text is historically CORRECT — but it means the MCC side sits one curator addition short of today's student layer ON TOP OF being 474-672 short of the F1 side. When ruling 20's unification is executed, do NOT treat this as '4,746 versus 4,746 plus phantoms'; the student baselines differ too.
metric_reference_asymmetry.gap_size: 474/5,220 = 9.08 % of the extended set at R = 50 m, rising to 672/5,418 = 12.4 % at 150 m — i.e. the F1 reference is 9.1-12.4 % larger than the MCC reference before the 4,745-versus-4,746 baseline difference is even counted.
